svg.title: Why a decision tree is easy to read
svg.desc: Twelve made-up students are shown, filled if they finished the term and hollow if not. A decision tree asks one yes-or-no question at a time. The first question, how many hours a week the student works, sends them down one of two branches. Those who work twenty hours or more are asked a second question, whether they have a study group. Each student ends up in one group, and you can read the path down to any group in plain words.

text.tspan: Filled: finished the term. Hollow: did not.
Twelve students. Some finished the term, some did not.
A decision tree asks one yes-or-no question at a time.
Each answer sends people down a branch.
Read down any branch to see who ended up there.
Every group can be explained in plain words.
